On Nov 23, US stocks surged led by a large jump in the Nasdaq after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Nvidia shares rose as much as 36.6% following his return; he had resigned on Nov 12 amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. President Donald Trump said he secured a deal to bring back Huang, who is widely seen as central to the AI trade.

The rally helped Wall Street recover from last week's selloff. On Nov 20, the S&P 500 and Dow both confirmed corrections amid growing worries about the AI trade. The Nasdaq-100 added more than US$2 trillion (S$2.3 trillion) in market value on Nov 23, while the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 posted their biggest daily gains since April 2025.

Preliminary data showed the S&P 500 gaining 328.45 points (4.75%) to close at 7,238.84; the Nasdaq Composite up 1,463.21 points (6.47%) to 24,080.94; and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 1,452.56 points (3.02%) to 49,599.89.

Before Nov 23, the Nasdaq had nearly entered a bear market as investors worried about heavy borrowing underpinning AI investment and questioned whether the sector could deliver sufficient returns; fears of political scrutiny also grew after Democrats swept the US midterm elections. On Monday, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index and S&P 500 information technology sector were sharply higher along with megacap stocks such as Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet.

Neocloud and data centre companies climbed too, having faced sharp selling pressure following Huang's abrupt exit; energy was the only group in negative territory. Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments, said "The thought had been... that Jensen Huang is uniquely important to Nvidia and to the AI trade," while noting one issue is resolved but how things play out remains to be seen.

Andrew Slimmon of Morgan Stanley Investment Management added: "We don't think the rebound has run its course, and at these levels, it's not too late to gradually add back technology exposure."

Ahead this week is Nov 25's personal consumption expenditures report, which could give clues about the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook.
items.title: US stocks surge as Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO

NVIDIA has released the general availability of its cuDSS library version 1.0, positioning it as a production-ready tool for solving large sparse linear systems in engineering and scientific simulations such as structural mechanics, computational fluid dynamics, circuit simulation, and power grid analysis.

The release emphasizes three technical pillars: advanced accuracy techniques that improve robustness on difficult symmetric indefinite systems; best-in-class performance delivering substantial speedups over CPU-based solvers; and a system-level optimization strategy anchored by host-assisted symbolic factorization, hybrid memory mode, and reduced GPU memory footprint. cuDSS is designed to scale across modern server nodes pairing an NVIDIA GPU with large amounts of CPU DRAM (often 512 GB to 2 TB), treating that memory as an extension of the device's effective capacity.

Benchmarking for the release used matrices drawn from semiconductor design, manufacturing, and computer-aided engineering workflows including circuit simulation, TCAD, thermal analysis, structural mechanics, electromagnetic problems, and fluid dynamics. These span a wide range of sparsity patterns, conditioning, and scaling behavior. On this configuration—cuDSS 1.0 speedup against Intel MKL version 2026.1.0; GPU: NVIDIA B200 (192 GB HBM3e); CPU: INTEL XEON PLATINUM 8570—the library reported geometric-mean speedups of 2.5x for analysis (reordering and symbolic factorization), 5.9x for numerical factorization, and 151x for triangular solve.

cuDSS performance has improved across releases: superpanels in factorization were optimized in v0.4.0, multithreaded analysis in v0.5.0, tuned solve-phase kernels in v0.8.0, and targeted optimizations in v1.0. Figures 4 and 5 show speedups relative to v0.3.0 through v1.0 for two matrices of significantly different sizes and structures.

For accuracy improvements on symmetric indefinite systems—which arise in optimal power flow, mixed finite element discretizations of fluid flow and porous media, PDE-constrained optimization, and interior mode computation—cuDSS now enables symmetry-preserving matching and scaling (using HSL MC64 from the HSL Mathematical Software Library) and Bunch-Kaufman pivoting by default. Matching was previously off because it did not preserve symmetry; it can add overhead if it causes additional fill-in, but setting CUDSS_CONFIG_FORCE_NONSYMMETRIC_MATCHING restores prior nonsymmetric behavior.

Bunch-Kaufman pivoting addresses accuracy loss from diagonal-only pivoting on matrices with small diagonals such as saddle-point and KKT systems. With CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN, cuDSS applies the local Bunch-Kaufman test to each column, choosing a 1×1 pivot, an interchanged 1×1 pivot, or a 2×2 block; the threshold can be overridden via CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_THRESHOLD. Smaller values favor 1×1 pivots for sparser factors at accuracy cost. Matching pairs with Bunch-Kaufman by splitting cycles into candidate groups that reordering keeps adjacent.

Table 1 reports results solving linear systems Ax = b under two configurations—no matching and diagonal pivoting versus matching/scaling plus Bunch-Kaufman pivoting—the latter now defaulting on SuiteSparse matrices from the collection with all-ones right-hand sides. The table measures Relative Residual, normwise relative backward error (NRBE), and perturbed 1×1 pivots; results show significant factorization improvement due to reduced perturbed pivots.

Test configuration: cuDSS 1.0, CTK13, RTX PRO 1000 Blackwell, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS) For these matrices, cuDSS is now up to 10 orders of magnitude more accurate in NRBE, with a stark reduction in perturbed pivots.

cuDSS 1.0 also enables matching and scaling by default for nonsymmetric matrices, not just symmetric and Hermitian ones; Table 2 shows SuiteSparse matrices that improve with matching enabled (test configuration: cuDSS 1.0, CTK13, RTX PRO 1000 Blackwell, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS). While generally helpful, matching can occasionally reduce accuracy and is disabled by setting the algorithm to CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE.

Hybrid memory mode orchestrates data placement across GPU HBM and CPU DRAM, keeping compute-intensive factorization and solve kernels on the GPU while offloading less-needed data. This lets engineers avoid partitioning simulations into subdomains or using multiple GPUs; the full problem solves as a single system. Figure 2 shows minimum memory requirements reduced by an average of 30% across large VLSI examples, enabling problems that previously required multiple GPUs to run on a single NVIDIA H100, B200, or Vera Rubin.

Users can query minimum device memory for hybrid mode via cudssDataGet() with CUDSS_DATA_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_MIN after the analysis phase; CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES provides a full breakdown including permanent and peak device memory (indices 0 and 1), minimum host memory, and maximum host memory. A custom limit can be set between that minimum and available free memory via cudaMemGetInfo using CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT.

Prior to cuDSS 1.0, pinned host buffers were registered by default through cudaHostRegister()/cudaFreeHost(), with the behavior controlled by CUDSS_CONFIG_USE_CUDA_REGISTER_MEMORY (default value = 1). Disabling registration can be faster for large systems due to overhead; cuDSS 1.0 introduces an opt-in user-configurable pinned memory handler via cudssSetPinnedMemHandler() that reduces latency and bandwidth overhead, allowing custom allocators such as pinned pools and parallel prefaulting.

Symbolic factorization determines the nonzero structure of factors and prepares data structures for numerical factorization; recent releases added GPU speedups and optional CPU offloading. In cuDSS 1.0, GPU symbolic factorization is 2.21x faster (geometric mean) than in v0.8.0 on both NVIDIA B200 and H100—the comparison covers ~400 matrix/configuration cases with 80 to 130.3 million rows on B200, and ~250 cases with 120 to 22.9 million rows on H100.

Replacing only symbolic factorization timings (holding reordering, numerical factorization, and solve at v0.8.0 values) gives estimated geometric-mean end-to-end speedups of 1.18x on B200 and 1.14x on H100. Optional host execution via hybrid execute mode was introduced in cuDSS 0.8 to help small matrices (reducing device overhead for otherwise host-based computation) and large matrices (reducing peak device memory during analysis). Users enable it before analysis with CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE; when disabled, symbolic factorization runs on the GPU.

For better host performance, users can set CUDSS_CONFIG_HOST_NTHREADS to allow more than one CPU thread. Hybrid execute mode and hybrid memory mode can now be enabled together in supported configurations: with both active, numerical factorization and solve use the GPU while symbolic factorization runs on the host (with hybrid memory disabled, an internal heuristic selects placement based on matrix structure).

NVIDIA states that as each new GPU architecture brings greater memory capacity, higher bandwidth, and faster interconnects, cuDSS algorithmic innovations will compound these advances to enable ever larger and more efficient solutions. The company offers a download link for users to get started.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases cuDSS 1.0, a Production-Ready GPU Sparse Linear Solver

items.summary: Rod Moshtagi and Sayash Kapoor of the Harvard Kennedy School argue that apocalyptic predictions about AI's impact on management consulting misunderstand both what clients pay for and how general-purpose technologies reshape demand. The authors contend that while AI already excels at analysis, it has yet to match human judgment in high-stakes decisions because strategic advice is a credence good whose quality depends heavily on execution factors outside the decision itself; even if AI closes this gap, firms still need humans to coordinate competing internal interests, lend credibility through reputation and relationships, and accept accountability for outcomes. The authors attribute these claims about consulting's five sources of value—analysis, judgment, coordination, credibility, and accountability—to their own framework built on prior analyses. They note that past general-purpose technologies like business computing, the internet, and cloud services similarly created new work for consultants rather than merely making existing work cheaper, citing a 1992 study by Paul Attewell on consultant-driven adoption of business computing, KPMG's e-business revenue rising from $678 million in fiscal 1999 to $1.11 billion in fiscal 2000, and Accenture partnering with AWS and Microsoft while Deloitte partnered with Google Cloud for cloud migrations. On AI specifically, the authors cite a BCG experiment showing consultants using GPT-4 completed product development tasks about 25% faster with higher quality work, note that strategy consulting spending contracted 2% in 2023 before recovering to 2.3% growth in 2025 and is forecast to grow 4% in 2026 (attributing this forecast to their own analysis), report that only about 10% of consulting revenue came from the public sector in 2023, quote McKinsey's Kate Smaje saying pure strategy work makes up less than 20% of the firm's work and clients increasingly want implementation expertise, cite a BCG January 2026 survey of nearly 2,400 executives expecting to double AI spending in 2026 with organizational execution as the main obstacle (attributing these surveys to BCG), report Accenture's $2.7 billion advanced AI revenue in fiscal 2025 tripling from the prior year and BCG reporting 25% year-over-year growth in AI services, note McKinsey advised on nearly 2,500 M&A transactions between 2013 and 2017 (attributing this to David Maister's "Grey Hair" concept), cite a March 2012 report of 4,250 IT and operations engagements through McKinsey's Business Technology Office launched in 1997, note KPMG Consulting's e-business work made up 47% of revenue by fiscal 2000 after expanding into internet consulting in 1999, cite Accenture working on more than 6,000 advanced AI projects in 2025 with its AI and data workforce growing from about 40,000 people in 2023 to about 77,000, note McKinsey's QuantumBlack employs about 1,700 people while BCG X employs nearly 3,000 technologists (attributing these figures to the firms themselves), and report that Accenture announced giving tens of thousands of professionals ChatGPT Enterprise in December 2025 followed by training about 30,000 on Anthropic's Claude. The authors recommend that consulting firms adapt by building know-how clients lack, developing in-house AI expertise while partnering with AI companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic (which have begun their own deployment businesses), and staying neutral across model providers to avoid conflicts of interest from token-based pricing.
items.title: Management consulting is not a thin wrapper on intelligence

items.summary: Brain-computer interface company Paradromics announced a partnership with Nvidia on Thursday to use the chipmaker's hardware and software for processing neural data. The collaboration centers on making Paradromics' implants more portable, which would help patients like Mary—a Michigan woman with motor neuron disease who uses a dime-sized implant containing more than 400 electrodes to communicate through synthesized speech—move away from bulky external electronics toward smaller devices that could eventually fit in a phone. Currently, the decoding process requires a cart of electronics plugged into an outlet, and Paradromics CEO Matt Angle described brain-computer interfaces as 'the ultimate case for edge computing,' processing data close to where it is generated rather than relying on distant cloud infrastructure. The company plans to use Nvidia's Jetson low-powered computing module so speech decoding can occur in a small device near the user, along with Holoscan AI sensor processing software to combine neural signals with other inputs like camera and microphone data while reducing lag time that could make conversation feel unnatural; Paradromics chief scientific officer Vikash Gilja said integrating Nvidia's foundation models locally would also help synthesized voices sound more human-like without requiring an internet connection. David Niewolny, Nvidia's director of business development for health care and medical, told WIRED via email that the technology processes neural signals and runs AI models in real time to adapt continuously as those signals change over time. The partnership comes amid a leadership shakeup at Nvidia following Jensen Huang's resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy; Niewolny noted that Nvidia is also working with other brain-computer interface companies including Synchron, though the chipmaker will not have access to brain data through these partnerships.
items.title: Paradromics Partners With Nvidia To Power Portable Brain-Computer Interfaces

items.summary: On Monday, Anthropic announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents designed to automate code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes. The company blog post explains that while existing AI coding tools already offered code review features, what is notable about Claude Ship is its inclusion of an agent capable of approving code changes automatically based on policies set by development teams. Anthropic states the launch arrives as AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving changes before they go live; with Claude Ship, the idea is to automate more of the development process by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself. A company blog post quotes Anthropic's reasoning: "Most teams want a person to approve every change... But a lot of developers build with agents now." The offering consists of Code Review, which is generally available, and two new beta agents—PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review, while also commenting after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back if needed. Claude Approvals applies an approval policy that teams write as a file in the repository, incorporating signals such as Code Review findings or company classifiers with policies written in natural language. Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first; teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits for more control. Anthropic says teams will remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human decision. The service is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub.
items.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship for Automated Code Reviews and Approvals

items.summary: Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning despite being caught in three affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy that has triggered multiple congressional investigations over national security concerns. Tech leaders celebrated the return: Elon Musk called it correcting a mistake and compared firing Huang to kicking Michael Jordan off a winning team, while Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao posted his support. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney said Jensen's return would demonstrate American resiliency to missteps, and former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick also voiced backing after both had themselves been driven out of companies they founded over scandals. Hedge fund manager Bill Ackman noted Nvidia's stock rebounded Monday morning as he argued the board was not acting in shareholders' best interests during Huang's ouster. Outside tech, elected officials remained skeptical about President Donald Trump's claims that Huang poses no national security risk; Senator John Cornyn asked what basis exists for such a claim, and Senator Pete Ricketts said Nvidia's decision does not excuse Huang from testifying before Congress or absolve the company of answering national security concerns. Huang is still expected to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, as well as privately before three House committees.
items.title: Jensen Huang Reinstated at Nvidia Amid National Security Scandal

An MIT study published in Nature Neuroscience reports that the human brain processes a wide range of languages through a shared neural mechanism, using artificial intelligence to reveal this commonality. The research team led by Evelina Fedorenko and Andrea Gregor de Varda used multilingual large language models—systems like those powering ChatGPT and Claude—to predict how the human brain responds to different languages, marking the first study to apply these models across many languages simultaneously.

The researchers built an AI encoding model that merges two data sources: numerical code from multilingual models representing sentences or phrases, and brain scans of people performing linguistic tasks. This tool predicts how the human brain lights up in response to language input by taking a model's representation of text and forecasting corresponding neural activity.

For this study, scientists combined preexisting brain imaging data from speakers of 12 languages—Afrikaans, Dutch, Farsi, French, Lithuanian, Marathi, Norwegian, Romanian, Spanish, Tamil, Turkish, and Vietnamese—with newly recruited participants speaking nine additional languages: Italian, Portuguese, German, Russian, Polish, Hindi, Arabic, Mandarin, and Korean. The team recorded brain activity while these 21 language speakers listened to stories from "Alice in Wonderland" in their native tongues.

The encoding models accurately predicted brain responses across all 21 studied languages, including Marathi and Lithuanian where limited data existed. Notably, a model trained on one language could predict neural responses for an untrained language—for instance, French-trained predictions applied to Vietnamese—suggesting brains represent language in a shared way.

The researchers attributed the common component they identified to meaning rather than surface-level linguistic features like tone or word order that vary significantly between languages. Fedorenko noted these differences exist but must still be represented somewhere in both brain and model systems, with future research potentially revealing how those distinctions are encoded.
items.title: MIT Study Finds Shared Neural Code for Language Across 21 Languages

items.summary: Anthropic announced in beta Monday that Claude can now review, fix, and approve pull requests as part of a new feature called Claude Ship, which partially automates the PR review process to help teams ship code faster. The feature uses two new agents—PR Steward and Claude Approvals—alongside Code Review, released in March for Teams and Enterprise plans. PR Steward participates in failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback but cannot approve or merge pull requests; it documents its changes through comments and provides instructions to undo them. Developers can guide the process by commenting @claude throughout. Claude Approvals references team policy provided as a repo file along with additional signals before approving changes autonomously if permitted, otherwise seeking deeper human sign-off. Anthropic recommends enabling these checks first in observe-only mode before configuring branch protection to require approval. The feature is available on Team and Enterprise plans via the /ship command in Claude Code, uses tokens that may affect billing, allows admins to set spending limits or enable it for entire repos without requiring the command, and excludes customers with zero-data-retention policies. Anthropic noted its own Claude Code team uses AI to write a majority of code needed. ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz said the concept raises concerns but acknowledged potential benefits like faster turnaround and cost savings, while also expressing worry about how it may affect younger developers' growth into senior decision-making roles.
items.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship Beta for Automated Code Review

items.summary: Microsoft warned customers that a vulnerability in Azure API Management (APIM) Classic tiers was exploited to steal stored API credentials, with Norwegian authorities linking the flaw to cyberattacks against energy companies. In an Azure Service Health security advisory (Tracking ID: MZK9-GH0), shared with BleepingComputer, Microsoft said it identified the vulnerability on November 18, 2026, and deployed a mitigation the following day. The company stated that its investigation found customers were exposed to unauthorized access to secrets stored in APIM Classic instances before the issue was identified. According to Microsoft, the flaw allowed unauthorized access to certain management functionality when APIM Classic instances were not configured according to recommended security best practices, potentially enabling attackers to perform administrative operations and access several categories of credentials: Named Values, client secrets associated with identity providers and OpenID Connect providers, subscription keys, and tokens used to call direct management APIs. Microsoft said it closed the unauthorized access path on November 19 and rotated its own controlled keys and credentials where appropriate, but warned that remediation would not invalidate customer credentials potentially compromised before the fix was deployed. The vulnerability affects APIM Classic tiers while v2 tiers are reportedly not impacted. In a Reddit post, an administrator claimed their organization discovered the vulnerability after detecting unauthorized access to Azure Key Vault using a valid administrator token; they alleged attackers exploited a zero-day authentication bypass in a deprecated legacy API to gain access to a privileged system account on APIM instances and that the legacy API did not generate logs for detection. BleepingComputer has not independently verified these allegations, which also included claims that Microsoft initially attributed suspicious activity to leaked customer credentials before deploying a global fix. The vulnerability was linked to attacks affecting Norwegian organizations including energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi; Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) said an unknown threat actor targeted access tokens, secrets, and named values stored in APIM, with the country's energy sector first discovering the flaw before it spread internationally. Equinor disclosed an ongoing cyberattack on November 17, a day before Microsoft identified the vulnerability, later announcing that it had stopped the attack with no indication of stolen or altered data; Skagerak Energi reported an attempted cyberattack but said there was no operational impact and no evidence information was compromised. While Microsoft's remediation required no customer action, NSM warned organizations to verify their APIM instances received the security update, noting that instances running below specific runtime versions remain vulnerable and advising customers to contact their service provider if they had not received it; it is unclear whether these runtime updates are separate from Microsoft's initial mitigation. Cloud security researcher Anders Kristiansen shared threat-hunting queries to help organizations investigate potential exploitation and identify stored credentials in APIM instances, while BleepingComputer reported that its questions about the attacks have yet to receive a reply from Microsoft.
items.title: Microsoft Warns Azure API Management Flaw Exploited to Steal Credentials

The suits follow a series of other legal actions against Musk's companies over similar issues, including cases brought by Baltimore and teens in Tennessee.

items.summary: Nvidia reversed its decision to remove Jensen Huang from his role, restoring him as president and CEO and board member just 11 days after he stepped down. The announcement came despite an ongoing independent investigation into whether Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence through a woman with whom he acknowledged having an affair, alongside allegations of at least one, possibly two, other affairs with subordinates during his absence. Nvidia's return also appears to have received the White House's tacit approval. In a statement upon returning, Huang said: 'I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution.' His reinstatement echoes Sam Altman's brief departure from OpenAI three years earlier, underscoring how central individual leaders have become to AI-focused firms. Kristy Loke, a research fellow at MATS studying China's role in global AI geopolitics and Nvidia's position within it, described the return as 'stunning,' noting that while it does not necessarily end chip debates in Washington, it highlights Jensen Huang's centrality as Nvidia's chief strategist and as the force holding together much of the AI ecosystem. Support for his reinstatement grew quickly across Silicon Valley over the past week: Elon Musk called for his return on November 14, warning that many of Nvidia's most important supply-chain deals rested on personal relationships with Huang rather than written contracts; Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick backed him, arguing his mistakes did not warrant removal from the company he built. By November 16, a petition calling for Huang's reinstatement had attracted more than 180,000 signatures, including those of Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Replit CEO Amjad Masad, as well as more than 8,800 people identifying themselves as Nvidia employees.
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Brief Absence Amid Scandals

items.summary: The U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) conducted covert tests earlier this year to determine whether users could bypass guardrails and convince major AI platforms—Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Grok—to plan terrorist attacks. The investigators succeeded: all four AIs produced attack scenarios that subject matter experts confirmed would have mostly succeeded. In October the agency published a report titled 'Covert Testing Used Common Platforms to Create Viable Attack Plans,' which was released to the public in November.
items.title: GAO Report Confirms Four AI Platforms Could Be Used to Plan Terrorist Attacks

items.summary: Databricks announced the general availability of a native sink connector that writes Apache Spark Structured Streaming computed results directly to its fully managed, serverless Lakebase PostgreSQL database. The connector handles batching, retries, connection pooling, deduplication, upserts, and workspace-managed authentication in both micro-batch and Real-Time Mode on Databricks Runtime 18 LTS and above (RealTime and ProcessingTime triggers run on classic compute; Trigger.AvailableNow is used on serverless), though it is not supported in Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines. It replaces the need for a custom foreach writer, which must manage batch writes, bounded queues for backpressure, connection pooling with OAuth token refresh, retry backoff, and correct upsert semantics such as keeping the greatest timestamp or updating only when an incoming event has a newer ordering value—work that can take weeks to build and then requires ongoing maintenance. Users write to Lakebase in minutes via a single writeStream call: .toTable() for Unity Catalog-registered tables (with automatic credential management and table creation), or format("postgresql") with the endpoint and dbtable for unregistered tables, which also supports external PostgreSQL databases like Amazon RDS on DBR 19+ Public Preview. The sink maintains one row per key via an upsertkey declaration and offers merge strategies in DBR 19+ to control how non-key columns update without hand-written ON CONFLICT SQL. Databricks demonstrated the connector on a recommendation feature pipeline that ingests watch and like events from a video streaming platform, computes each user's last-6 watched videos and last-3 liked items via transformWithState, and upserts one row per user into Lakebase within 100-200 milliseconds of production for single-digit millisecond serving. In testing the pipeline sustained ~20K events/sec against 5 million active users on a 40-core classic compute cluster (DBR 18 LTS) writing to an 8-CU Lakebase project with 5-minute RTM checkpoint intervals, performing upserts that continuously overwrite each user's feature row as state grows. At this throughput the sink executed 63.5 million upserts averaging ~0.015 milliseconds per statement on pg_stat_statements, according to Databricks.
items.title: Databricks Announces General Availability of Native Lakebase Postgres Sink for Spark Structured Streaming

items.summary: US President Donald Trump left his November visit to Manila without concluding an agreement on New Clark City, part of the US-led Pax Silica initiative. The Philippine ambassador to Washington told Reuters that nothing had been signed; instead, the US made a broad offer to supply food and energy with terms still to be worked out. The Philippines joined Pax Silica in April, but that declaration did not settle the terms for New Clark City, the proposed 4,000-acre industrial hub in Tarlac. Before the bilateral meeting, Philippine President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos said the hub was not on the agenda; trade officials still aim for a framework by year-end, and there is time for the public to shape it if Manila permits. The White House announced a separate cloud partnership that includes modernizing the Philippine defense cloud. CSIS notes Trump floated cooperation on nuclear power and an Alaska gas pipeline. None of these actions settles how New Clark City will be governed, what investors will owe, or what happens to people living there.
items.title: Trump Left Manila Without a Pax Silica Deal. What Can the Philippines Demand?

items.summary: In response to Desmond Wai Chun Tao's November 16 letter urging cybersecurity protections before further integrating medical records, Goh Min Liong of the Ministry of Health clarified that the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) does not replace healthcare providers' own electronic medical record systems. According to MOH, hospitals and clinics continue to maintain their own clinical records and rely primarily on these systems for patient care. The NEHR instead brings together key health information—such as medications, allergies, discharge summaries, and investigation results—to help professionals make better-informed decisions when patients receive care across different providers, which is especially important for those with multiple conditions treated at separate institutions to avoid missed details, repeated investigations, or delayed treatment. MOH acknowledged that cybersecurity risks are evolving and stated the NEHR is protected through multiple layers of security, ongoing monitoring, regular penetration testing, and independent cybersecurity audits, describing cybersecurity as an ongoing effort rather than a one-off exercise while pledging continued strengthening of safeguards for patient information and continuity of care during system disruptions. The statement also encouraged healthcare providers to take proactive steps to ensure their own systems have sufficient cybersecurity and data security measures.
items.title: MOH Clarifies NEHR Safeguards Key Health Information Without Replacing Provider Records

items.summary: In an opinion piece dated November 23, 2026, Janet Haven argues that the recent midterm election results gave voters a clear mandate against tech industry power and in favor of AI controls. The author contends that while Americans voted for candidates promising oversight of artificial intelligence and its developers, Congress has repeatedly failed to act on public demands due to longstanding tendencies—across both parties—to cave to the tech industry's money, access, and arguments that regulation would harm innovation or national security. Haven cites several examples of this inaction: despite the 2018 Cambridge Analytica scandal involving Facebook allowing data harvesting from up to 87 million users, no federal data privacy law has been enacted; following ChatGPT's launch and mainstream discussion of existential AI risk, bipartisan Congressional leadership created the AI Insight Forums in 2023 but failed to produce legislation; and Senator Chuck Schumer's 2024 roadmap document was described as anodyne guidance rather than actual legislative action. The author notes that incentives for industry opposition remain strong, pointing to Jensen Huang's conflicts of interest regarding Nvidia chip exports to China as a national security concern. Haven concludes by urging the incoming Democratic Congress to pursue holistic AI governance protecting safety and rights, participate in international standards-setting, and take steps to prevent catastrophic risk through legislation, public spending, and new authorities rather than accepting industry-friendly self-regulation.
items.title: Newly Empowered Democrats Urged to Avoid Repeating Congress's Tech Governance Failures

This Hugging Face guide explains how to build, validate, share, and maintain agentic AI evaluations. It argues that open-source evaluation infrastructure—tasks, environments, harnesses, verifiers, traces, and evidence—should be shared so others can scrutinize results, correct errors, and reuse them, even when active test items are held back to prevent contamination.

The article frames evaluation design as having evolved through three eras: question-answer benchmarks (e.g., MMLU in 2020, GPQA in 2023), agentic benchmarks that score what an agent changed in an environment (e.g., SWE-bench and WebArena), and team or swarm benchmarks that assess coordinated multi-agent output. It focuses on agentic evaluations because they are increasingly prominent in model release announcements due to enterprise interest, and because their design offers a clear starting point for understanding how evaluation setup affects scores.

The guide walks through eight steps of building one agentic evaluation: define the claim; find or adapt an existing task; run it unchanged as a baseline; adapt it for domain needs; check the evaluation itself against reference solutions, no-op agents, and cheating shortcuts; read traces to diagnose failures beyond raw scores; report the score with appropriate metrics; and compare models. The walkthrough is applied to raman-lab, where builders reused Terminal-Bench's raman-fitting task and the Harbor harness rather than starting from scratch.

The article reports that in an audit of Terminal-Bench, researchers kept a model fixed while changing only the agent harness and saw accuracy vary by up to 29.9 percentage points. In its own example, on eight adapted tasks it ran three rollouts per task (24 total), with the setup passing 11 of 24; gpt-oss-120b passed 0 of 3 in a baseline run and later 13 of 24 when DeepInfra was pinned as provider. It reports pass@3 of 7/8, pass^3 of 1/8, and a clustered mean pass rate of 0.46 with a standard error of about 0.11.

The guide documents that errors in tasks and graders are common: a review found flaws could shift measured performance by up to 100% relative terms; Terminal-Bench 2.1 fixed 28 of its 89 tasks after user reports, including one whose tests expected Spark SQL while instructions asked for PostgreSQL; CritPt's auditors had to solve problems themselves before finding errors in 21 of the 56 challenges they reviewed because reference solutions were private; OpenAI's audit of SWE-bench Verified found material issues in 59.4% of its 138 problems; and in July 2026 OpenAI estimated about 30% of SWE-Bench Pro tasks were broken, withdrawing its recommendation to adopt it.

On contamination versus saturation, the article notes that 98.2% of model-benchmark scores are reported by only one party, Artificial Analysis says 60% of its Intelligence Index v5 (announced October 2026) rests on evaluations with private test sets or held-out answers, and Google DeepMind piloted double-blind evaluations in August 2026. It argues that withholding materials does not guarantee quality and can hinder expert review.

The guide presents a table outlining what to open strategically for each evaluation component—task format, task data, environment, agent harness, rollout/trace records, reference solution, evaluation harness, and verifier—and notes how existing benchmarks vary in openness: ARC-AGI-2 publishes training and 120-task sets while holding back two semi-private/private sets of 120 tasks each; AILuminate keeps official prompts confidential but publishes methods and taxonomy with evidence available for controlled review by authorized auditors; Terminal-Bench marks task files with a canary string. It also reports that the saturation study rated 29 of its 60 language model benchmarks as highly saturated, with rates rising with age.

Finally, it argues that open evaluations have an 'afterlife': tasks become regression checks for new harnesses, environments and verifiers seed harder successors, and benchmarks get repaired and reissued—citing MMLU becoming MMLU-Redux and Terminal-Bench 2.0 becoming 2.1 through community contributions—and concludes that shared evaluation work can outlive the benchmark itself.
items.title: How to Build and Maintain an Agentic Evaluation

items.summary:
On November 23, 2026, the Ladybird project released its first alpha browser for macOS and Linux users without requiring compilation. The article notes that Ladybird implements most core components—HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, and WebAssembly—while relying on external libraries such as HarfBuzz, Skia, ffmpeg, and SQLite. During testing, the author reported it felt fast with a lightweight interface and successfully loaded several websites, including running an ffmpeg-based video compressor, an image-resize tool, and a Pyodide Python REPL compiled to WebAssembly. However, Datasette Lite failed with an error: 'undefined is not a function (evaluated from navigator.serviceWorker.startMessages)', which the author filed as an issue before finding a FIXME annotation in the source code.

The article attributes recent progress partly to coding agents. On February 23, 2026, Andreas Kling published 'Ladybird adopts Rust', describing how AI tools helped port about 25,000 lines of LibJS JavaScript engine from C++ to Rust within two weeks. A GitHub contributions chart over twelve months shows an uptick in October corresponding to major improvements described in the project's 'This Month in Ladybird — October 2026' post: moving style and layout to their own thread, landing a new JavaScript JIT, replacing the C++ engine with Cranelift WebAssembly (achieving a 7x boost on the JetStream 3 WASM benchmark), and gaining about 75,650 new passes on roughly 2.25 million subtests in the web-platform-tests suite—beating Safari.

The author attributes most of that October gain to AI coding agents: WebPlatformTests grew from about 2.12 million on October 22 to about 2.18 million on October 27, with roughly 30,000 new passes in /css and about 10,000 in /editing over five days as the project pointed AI agents at WPT to fill missing functionality.

Regarding which models were used for that surge, the author speculates they are uncertain—Andreas reportedly uses Codex and Claude Code—but notes Claude Opus 5.5 released September 22, 2026 and Claude Fable 5.2 on November 9, 2026 (afterward), so no specific versions have been confirmed.

On usability, the article quotes Andreas Kling warning that as an alpha some websites may not work and crashes can occur; users are encouraged to report broken sites from within the browser or submit crash reports after a failure. The project also invites security researchers to test it openly while making no security guarantees. The author declines to use Ladybird for sensitive accounts like GitHub or Gmail but plans to keep using it for anonymous browsing, partly to support testing efforts and citing optimism about growth in what they describe as a stagnant browser engine market.
items.title: Ladybird Browser Releases First Alpha and Reports October Coding-Agent Gains

items.summary: James White and Nora Söderberg of Lund University's Department of Technology and Society respond to Steve Rose's November 12 letter, arguing that his characterization of Sweden as a place where datacentres are not politically contentious misrepresents the reality. They point to the proposed Google development at Torsboda near Sundsvall—which requires substantial electricity and industrial land—as evidence of significant controversy, noting that Norrlandspartiet's StoppaGoogle campaign has actively challenged concerns about its effects on electricity prices, employment, and regional development. The authors contend that this dispute reflects broader debates over resource extraction for the green and technological transitions, including fears that Sweden is becoming an 'electricity colony' of big tech supplying cheap green energy while economic benefits accrue elsewhere. Drawing on research by Julia Velkova, Jutta Haider, and Malte Rödl, they argue that digital infrastructure's sustainability cannot be reduced to carbon emissions or efficiency alone; instead, datacentres place heavy demands on electricity grids requiring government investment at the expense of other industries, communities, and public services. The scholars conclude that Sweden's renewable energy does not render datacentre development unproblematic but generates distinct tensions over who controls, benefits from, and gains access to natural and public resources—conflicts shaped by differing histories, infrastructures, and political economies rather than representing an exception to the growing politicisation of such projects.
items.title: Lund Scholars Refute Claim That Sweden's Datacentre Politics Are Uncontentious

items.summary: The U.S. Army plans to detonate nearly five tons of lead azide, a volatile primary explosive used to make bombs, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday, using an emergency provision under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act to bypass a court-ordered pause on its EPA permit. Dozens of barrels stored for decades have reformed into crystals highly sensitive to friction and shock; the Army argues that freezing temperatures will make them even more unstable and must dispose of them before winter sets in. A Department of Justice brief filed with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 8th Circuit on Sunday states that a permit is not necessary for emergency action against an immediate threat from explosive material, while also asserting controlled detonation minimizes lead dust release compared to any alternative handling or waiting.
items.title: Army Seeks to Detonate Lead Explosives in Iowa Despite Court-Ordered Permit Pause

items.summary: At the recent DealBook Summit, Elon Musk said that “the number of lives that have been saved” by Starlink connectivity “may be hundreds,” and when host Andrew Ross Sorkin asked for specifics he replied, “It’s all over the internet. Just do a search.” The article notes this comment was ill-placed given reports that Ukraine has suffered repeated disruptions to its access to Starshield — the military version of SpaceX's Starlink. In an editorial following President Donald J. Trump's meeting with Russian President Putin and Chinese President Xi, former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton reminded readers that, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian access to US early warning intelligence about incoming Russian missile strikes has been fractured and Ukraine's access to Starshield remains limited; the article states that limited Starshield access means increased Ukrainian deaths as it battles Russia. Musk addressed restrictions on the Ukrainian military during the summit, saying Starlink was never meant for offensive use in war. Historian Rebecca Solnit argued against dismissing Musk's handling of Ukrainian airspace as mere commerce, stating he “has made much of his obscene pile of money off the US government with SpaceX and StarLink” and has been given power that should not belong to individuals by manipulating Starlink in ways impairing Ukraine; she described him as having returned to such manipulation. Representative Jim Himes (D-CT), top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, wrote Musk a formal request “that senior SpaceX officials meet with me to explain the Starshield service disruptions in Ukraine in October 2026,” noting that because SpaceX is “a US Government purchased service established via a contract between the U.S. Government and SpaceX” and has potentially modified it unilaterally along with its lack of responsiveness to congressional oversight, every such government contract should be questioned; Himes asked why those changes were made and whether they were directed by a US Government official. Musk also insisted Starlink is “revolutionary,” saying its design can be placed on a roof so people in buildings are reached, and proposed micro-ground stations as an alternative to metal roofs or big cell towers for making the network ubiquitous; he acknowledged gaps in service continue but said this was “the missing piece of the puzzle.” Former Secretary of Labor Robert Reich described Musk as one of the “authoritarians of the new economy” with “unparalleled power over every aspect of the lives of Americans and millions of others around the world,” and suggested Democrats investigate why Musk funneled a half-billion dollars into the 2026 midterms, questioning whether it was to keep his satellite monopoly or defense contracts. When Sorkin reminded him that Musk once said his “mind was like a storm,” Musk replied he currently feels “relatively at peace.”
items.title: Elon Musk Defends Starlink at DealBook Summit Amid Criticism Over Ukraine Access

items.summary:
The 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey collapsed after roughly two weeks of negotiations that ran nearly 50 hours into overtime—the longest ever—when more than 90 nations, including the Marshall Islands, the United Kingdom, and the entire European Union, objected to a draft high-level political agreement known as a cover decision. The rejected draft omitted the words 'fossil fuels' and left key details about climate finance unaddressed. Irish climate minister Darragh O'Brien stated during a closing plenary that his delegation would not endorse an Antalya pact or cover decision that does not mention fossil fuels, adding that the EU cannot accept it because the draft fails to address the climate emergency.

The talks were run by ministers from Turkey and Australia in an unusual arrangement. It was the first climate conference since COP15 in 2009 to founder over a cover decision, with many nations blaming shoddy management by the hosts. The breakdown occurred as the world approached permanently exceeding 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) of warming, with a historic El Niño expected to intensify impacts.

Delegates clashed on multiple fundamental issues beyond fossil fuels and climate finance. Petrostates including Saudi Arabia and Russia blocked any affirmation of the COP28 transition commitment and defeated language establishing a target for electricity to generate 35 percent of global energy by 2035, up from 23 percent today. More than 130 nations backed that electrification pledge before it was scuttled; Turkish environmental minister Murat Kurum had pitched the move as strategically important given the Iran war's disruption of petroleum through the Strait of Hormuz.

The cover decision became the central focus, drawing heavy attention from the presidency while countries like Russia rejected a summary document. Alden Meyer of E3G noted there was never before a cover decision so focused upon and resoundingly rejected by such a significant group of countries. Imane Saidi of the Imal Initiative argued that bundling issues into one package lowers ambition to the lowest denominator.

Climate finance stalled as well, with Turkey and Australia making no substantial pledges and the Adaptation Fund raising just $50 million—one-sixth of its annual target. Joe Thwaites of the Natural Resources Defense Council said developed countries engaged in finger-pointing over how to fairly share effort, while a COP presidency that made no own finance pledge lacked credibility.

On climate governance, draft texts expressed deep concern about breaching 1.5 degrees Celsius and reaffirmed commitments to limit extra warming and time above it. However, the cover decision also supported carbon capture, utilization, and sequestration (CCUS), which green groups and some scientists call a false solution that could prolong fossil fuel dependence. Between 1972 and 2018, nearly 90 percent of planned CCUS projects never got built, while those completed mostly used captured carbon to extract more oil.

MIT professor Charles Harvey called CCUS 'a disaster for the climate' and said he was suspicious of its prominence in COP31 draft texts given fossil fuel industry promotion. Advocates and European diplomats said the technology had been parachuted into COP31 by fossil fuel interests, particularly Saudi Arabia; one analysis counted 700 carbon capture lobbyists registered for COP31—more than the 699 delegates from G7 countries.

Other negotiations also failed: countries could not agree on just transition policies or establish a baseline to triple adaptation finance by 2035 as agreed last year, and opposition led to expiration of a standalone forum for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Delegates also failed to set an IPCC timeline for its seventh assessment; green groups want it before the 2028 global stocktake while Saudi Arabia objected over safeguarding the scientific process.

Diplomats may pick up deferred issues in June during technical talks in Germany, in unscheduled informal negotiations, or at COP32 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Ali Mohamed, a lead negotiator for an African bloc writing to Grist, said the lack of consensus cannot be delinked from global geopolitics where nationalism and protectionism upend multilateralism.

COP31's failure may intensify reform efforts; Erika Lennon of the Center for International Law noted shifting mood after unusually high attendance at a rules-of-procedure event. Sébastien Duyck said no one can now show up to the next COP claiming the same ridiculous rules will work, and that you cannot let any one of 195 countries hold the world hostage.

Meanwhile, frustrated nations are seeking action outside formal negotiations: sixty countries met in Santa Marta, Colombia earlier this year for the first fossil fuel transition conference, with the next slated for July in Tuvalu. Nearly 30 countries have roadmaps to transition away from fossil fuels building on a Brazil-promoted process.
items.title: COP31 Collapses Over Omitted Fossil Fuel Language

items.summary:
Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after US President Donald Trump intervened directly with the company's board of directors, in a reversal less than two weeks after he resigned. Speaking on Monday shortly after Nvidia announced his return, Trump said he had 'convinced' the board to restore him and told CNBC that he 'made the deal.' Huang had originally stepped down following reports of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang—whom US authorities suspect is spying for China—and two other Nvidia employees. In a statement after his reinstatement, Huang said: 'I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution.'

Nvidia shares surged on Monday following the announcement, jumping 32% and adding more than $1tn (£760bn) to the company's market value. Trump said 'the country needs Jensen's leadership,' while Nvidia stated its board had talked with Huang and was 'satisfied with respect to Mr Huang's candor and ability to lead.' The reinstatement marked a sharp reversal from the board's decision days earlier to rule out his return, according to reports.

The US vice-president, JD Vance, played a key role in discussions between the White House, Huang, and Nvidia, per the New York Times. On the same day as Huang's reinstatement, the US government announced it had added Megaspeed—a Singapore-based company formerly run by Alice Huang—to a federal trade blacklist over suspected diversion of semiconductors in breach of export controls amid concerns about chips being smuggled to China. Trump said Monday that the US government had no 'evidence that [Jensen Huang] has engaged in any unlawful conduct' and that attorney general Todd Blanche felt Huang was 'exonerated.'

Trump told CNBC that the country must 'protect our geniuses,' noting Chinese President Xi Jinping praised Huang at last week's Apec summit in Shenzhen. He said he had been speaking to Nvidia directors directly and indirectly, feeling strongly about his return as events unfolded with the company.

Nvidia shares had fallen by a quarter in the days after Huang resigned on 12 November, mirroring a wider AI rout in global stock markets that week as investors feared new leadership could dampen prospects for companies relying on Nvidia's chips. News of his reinstatement sparked a broader rally across Wall Street, sending the Nasdaq composite index up 6.5% and the S&P 500 by 4.7%, while lifting the US dollar to a 19-month high.

Senator Elizabeth Warren called the decision 'reckless,' saying it did not change that Huang owed Congress answers about Nvidia's compliance with trade restrictions, noting he is due to give evidence on 1 December and that California is investigating whether Nvidia chips reached China. She said his return increased urgency for Congress to pass export control bills and ensure Nvidia does not lobby against such legislation.

Nvidia stated an independent investigation into allegations Huang was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation remains ongoing 'and will proceed to conclusion.' Harvey Jones, Nvidia's chair appointed this month after Huang's resignation, said: 'The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.'

Huang built Nvidia from a video-game chip designer into the dominant supplier of AI processors. His return came hours after reports that Alice Huang had been in contact with an official in China's spy agency during their affair; people with knowledge of US intelligence reports claimed she remained in touch until this autumn, per the New York Times.

The Arm Holdings chief executive Rene Haas—who had been approached to succeed Huang—has signed a new deal keeping him in his current role until 2033. Elon Musk, who called for Huang's return in an open letter backed by other Silicon Valley figures, posted on X: 'Welcome back the main man,' alongside a picture of himself shaking hands with Huang; Trump said he had spoken to Musk over the last week or so about the situation.

Sam North, a market analyst at eToro, commented that Jensen Huang's return 'underlines how much of the AI trade still rests on one man.' The reinstatement echoes another recent Silicon Valley drama: OpenAI brought back its chief executive Sam Altman almost three years to the day prior. Altman was removed by his board on 17 November 2023 but restored five days later following an internal power battle, and in a Monday post he wrote 'Jensen!'
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Trump Intervention

items.summary:
Nvidia's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang less than two weeks after his ouster over revelations of multiple affairs, including with a suspected Chinese spy. The move followed intense pressure from Nvidia partners who feared his handshake deals would collapse and stock that soared 35% on his return.

The central development is why Huang won the power struggle: he sat at the center of an ecosystem where buyers, suppliers, and financiers depended on his word and vision. Nvidia finances much of the AI build-out rather than just selling into it. It has invested $30 billion in OpenAI, which buys computing from Nvidia's customers; put $2 billion into CoreWeave, a customer renting Nvidia-powered computing to developers; agreed to buy CoreWeave's unsold capacity through 2032 at an initial value of $6.3 billion; gives large customers 3-12 months to pay; and committed up to $10 billion to Anthropic, which in turn committed to buy $30 billion of computing from Microsoft's Azure.

Nvidia also lends its credit standing through guarantees lenders and landlords rely on—up to $118 billion total, including up to $105 billion backing OpenAI's leases at SB Energy's Ohio data-center campus—and is working with Blackstone, Apollo, KKR and others to raise more than $500 billion of outside capital.

This circular financing carries risk: if demand for computing power falls behind supply, Nvidia would absorb losses as seller, investor, backstop buyer, and guarantor simultaneously. Its share price could fall sharply, dragging down the market and tightening credit elsewhere in the economy. Counterparties saw Huang as the personal guarantor of this fragile system.

In March, speaking of TSMC, Huang said: "I don't know how many tens, hundreds of billions of dollars of business we've done through them, and we don't have a contract." Suppliers invest upstream because he told CEOs about the industry's size. Two days after Huang resigned following revelations including an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Elon Musk said on social media that "many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract."

The author argues finance is 10% math and 90% psychology. A Machiavellian reading holds that Huang planned his resignation as a springboard back: by resigning first he took the sting out of future revelations and let everyone feel life without him. Nvidia's stock was hammered around his departure, all three major market indexes ended last week in correction territory, partners assembled a "war room" to lobby for his return, and the board chair said during an earnings call that Huang wasn't coming back—six days later he was.

The board outsourced its judgment to Washington, saying senior levels of the U.S. government assured it Huang posed no national security risk; Trump called his intervention "very important," viewing Huang as an ace in the AI race with China. The board had cited Huang's lack of candor but now declared itself satisfied and reinstated him before its own investigation concluded—a climbdown scored 2-1 for Huang.

Huang offered humility and thanks to his family but no fresh apology, while Nvidia announced a search for a chief compliance officer reporting to a board committee. Almost 200,000 people signed a petition for his return, more than 10,000 of whom said they were Nvidia employees.

The author concludes that figures like Huang come as a single package: genius and limits inseparable. They live in the world of ideas rather than people, which frees them to break rules and norms; institutions exist to check them—and at Nvidia, the institution lost.

items.summary: Pawel Janas's NBER Working Paper 36040 documents the integration of the American capital market between 1870 and 1940, using what it describes as the first long-run, geolocated, firm-level record of asset holdings by large institutional investors: more than 100,000 bond holdings held by life insurers over that period. The paper finds that between 1880 and 1890, the mean distance of insurers' bonds from their home states more than doubled, while their share of home-state holdings fell from over half to under a quarter. This shift occurred within firms, across bond classes, and across charters. Janas reports that mortgage lending was national wherever state law permitted it, and concludes that capital market integration among life insurers was largely complete by 1890.
items.title: The Emergence of a National Capital Market (1870–1940)

items.summary: A study by Sarah Eichmeyer, Aljoscha Janssen, and Jonathan Zhang (NBER Working Paper 36041) investigates whether treating addiction improves both economic circumstances and health. Using two decades of Veterans Health Administration records on over 140,000 patients with opioid use disorder combined with consumer credit data, the authors exploit staggered facility-level buprenorphine adoption and quasi-random emergency physician assignment to examine treatment effects.
items.title: Treating Addiction Rebuilds Lives: Evidence from Buprenorphine

items.summary: The European Commission has launched a WTO-announced safeguard investigation into certain composite input materials, notified under document G/SG/N/6/EU/6. A safeguard investigation seeks to determine whether increased imports of a product are causing or threatening to cause serious injury to a domestic industry; if such injury is found, a WTO member may temporarily restrict imports of the product.
items.title: EU launches safeguard investigation into certain composite input materials

items.summary: The United States added Singapore-based chip firm Megaspeed to its trade blacklist on Monday (Nov 23), the company closely tied to an espionage investigation involving Nvidia. The move follows revelations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, Megaspeed's controlling shareholder and a Chinese businesswoman reportedly alleged to be a spy for Beijing; Reuters could not independently verify this intelligence allegation, which China has called "groundless." The blacklist addition coincided with Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO after his resignation two weeks earlier over reports of extramarital affairs. Under US rules, companies cannot ship goods, software and technology to entities on the list without a license that is likely to be denied, making it harder for listed firms to access US-origin spare parts, software updates or intellectual property licenses; Megaspeed did not immediately respond to comment requests. The New York Times reported last month that US authorities concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset who passed information to Beijing while developing her relationship with the Nvidia CEO. People familiar with the matter said Alice Huang led Megaspeed, historically one of Nvidia's largest chip customers; she left the company in August 2025 and it has stated it conducted "lawful business." US authorities have investigated Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, according to the Justice and Commerce departments this week. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a Nov 8 statement following reports without referring to Alice Huang by name. The last time the Commerce Department placed new entities on the list was October 2025; Reuters reported in June that the US has held off adding China's AI startup DeepSeek, memory chipmaker CXMT and more than 100 other companies flagged as national security risks while the Trump administration sought to avoid escalating tensions with Beijing.
items.title: US Blacklists Singapore Chip Firm Megaspeed Over Nvidia Espionage Investigation

items.summary: US stocks surged on Monday (Nov 23), led by a big jump in the Nasdaq, after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. The move drove investors back into AI-related shares following last week's selloff. Nvidia's shares rose as much as 36.6 per cent after the board returned Huang, who had resigned on Nov 12 amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. US President Donald Trump said he secured a deal to bring back Huang as CEO.
items.title: Wall Street Jumps Back as Jensen Huang Returns as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: Nvidia announced the immediate reinstatement of its founder and chief executive, Jensen Huang, sending Wall Street sharply higher. The Nasdaq rose about 6.5%, while the S&P 500 gained roughly 4.8% and the Dow climbed around 3.1%. Nvidia's stock reportedly jumped approximately 32% on the news. Analysts had partly attributed a recent losing streak in the tech index to the crisis surrounding Huang, whose departure this month followed revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a businesswoman US authorities suspected of spying for China; Beijing denied those allegations and Nvidia said its board unanimously voted to reinstate him after being satisfied with his candour and leadership ability. The move comes just days after the board had ruled out Huang's return.
items.title: Wall Street Rallies as Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang

items.summary: A riverine healthcare program in Rio Branco, capital of Brazil's Acre state, faces an uncertain future amid longer droughts and drier rivers in the Brazilian Amazon. The initiative has operated for more than 20 years, with crews of up to 70 professionals sailing along the Riozinho do Rôla through roughly 11 outreach sites serving about 150 communities across its rural area. Despite this two-decade history that helped nearly eradicate malaria locally — Acre recorded just 18 locally acquired cases in 2025 and saw a 60% drop between 2021 and 2025 — the program's future is now at risk as climate change turns vital waterways into impassable mud. According to the November bulletin of the Drought and Immobility Risk in the Amazon Basin report, river levels across the Brazilian Amazon are below or far below average, with six of Acre's 22 municipalities having more than 20 communities under threat of drought-induced immobility.
items.title: Longer droughts threaten floating health clinics as Amazon streams run dry
